newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends dull session tightly mixed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends dull session tightly mixed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended narrowly mixed in uneventful dealings on Friday.
"It was a very slow session," said one trader. "The market just seems to be in a holding pattern waiting to see what develops with the (Brazil) weather next week."

September coffee rose 0.45 cent per lb firmer, at 184.95 cents, after ranging from 187.00 to 183.25 cents. Second-month December fell 0.25 cent, to 162.30 cents, while the back months closed down 0.25 to 1.05 cents.
The September/December switch widened to 22.65 cents compared with 21.95 cents at the close on Thursday.
Coffee prices rose at the outset, defying a 1.00-cent lower pre-opening call, on some commission house short-covering, dealers said. Light trade selling, however, capped gains, they aaded.
Some dealers said weather forecasts citing a slight possibility of a freeze in top-grower Brazil provided some underlying support.

Weather forecaster Cropcast said Friday long-range guidance models showed the greatest threat of cold weather reaching Brazil's coffee belt will be toward the middle of next week, with the probability of a freeze set at 20 percent.

However, forecaster Weather Services Corp said in its daily update today that while somewhat cooler temperatures could reach Brazil's coffee belt during the second half of the week, a high pressure expected to build in Argentina next week is likely to pass well to the south of coffee growing areas.
Traders said today's September options expiry was relatively orderly, with many operators unloading postions on Thursday.

Additionally, fund interest in the market remained light, they said, with open interest still very low. As of July 31, total open interest stood at 21,794 lots, down 208 lots from the previous session.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 190.00 cents, while support was seen at 181.00 cents.

On the fundamental side, a report published by German statistician F.O. Licht on Friday said world coffee consumption could rise by 15 million bags over the next decade but new markets are needed for any appreciable growth.
World consumption is estimated at 100 million bags in 1996/97, it said.
After Friday's close the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 3,092 60-kg bags as of July 31, to 95,491 bags. An additional 250 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume on the day was meager, at an estimated 2,636 lots.
